method.generation: short prompt (one sentence), 800 output tokens, temperature 0, mean of 2 runs
method.end_to_end: ~16,850 input tokens, 800 output tokens, 1 run; tokens/s = completion_tokens / total wall time, so prefill is included
method.warmup: two short requests discarded after each server start — without them the first measurement pays CUDA graph capture and JIT (Nemotron read 62.8 instead of 78.7)
method.prefix_cache: the long prompt carries a fixed-width per-model prefix so a previous model cannot produce a cache hit; the body is character-identical for every model
method.caveat: tokens are counted by each model own tokenizer. The same filler text is 16,849 tokens for the Qwen family and 20,483 for Laguna, so cross-family tokens/s comparisons understate the coarser tokenizer.
method.same_model_two_precisions: qwen36moe (FP8, 35 GB) and qwen36nvfp4 (NVFP4, 23 GB) are the same model at two precisions, measured with the same method: 50.0 against 78.3 tok/s generating, 1.57x. Not the 2x that halving the bytes per weight suggests — attention, routing and the KV cache (FP8 in both) do not shrink with the weights.
method.long_prompt_instruction: the long prompt ends with an explicit request for a 900-word text. Without it a model answers filler with two sentences: Ornith produced 116 output tokens and read 29.4 tok/s, while its prefill runs at about 6,000 tok/s. The end-to-end number is completion_tokens over wall time, so it measures terseness unless the output actually reaches the cap. tools/throughput.py implements the method.
